summary: All 7 phases across 4 waves complete. Extensions.json relocated to preset-scoped project-root dotfiles (.claude-extensions.json / .opencode-extensions.json) via config.lua's new root_state_file field at the single state.lua get_state_path choke point; all shell readers (skill-base.sh, validate-wiring.sh) and their .claude/.opencode deployed copies updated in lockstep. manager.regenerate (init.lua) reads the surviving manifest's active extensions, resets state, and reloads each via manager.load, whose existing recursive dependency resolution handles ordering. settings.json/settings.local.json keep their hardcoded .claude/ path (host-app constraint): loader.lua's copy_root_files gained an install-once guard, and a post-hoc gap was found and closed where manager.unload was deleting these files before install-once could ever apply on the next load, defeating it for the unload-then-load reload cycle. A new settings_backup.lua module provides true zero-loss across a full wipe (backup -> rm -rf base_dir -> regenerate -> restore), wired into manager.regenerate. logs/ relocated to project-root .agent-logs/ across 5 source scripts and all deployed copies. Documentation swept in EXTENSION.md, README.md, extension-system.md, permission-configuration.md, and the literature extension's README.md. Phase 7 proved the full cycle headlessly in scratchpad fake project dirs: 20/20 assertions passed, all 292 pre-wipe files reproduced byte-identically post-regenerate (modulo a discovered pre-existing, out-of-scope index.json key-order non-determinism), and the real ~/.config/nvim/.claude tree was never touched destructively. check-extension-docs.sh (the hard orphan/broken-symlink gate) passes after every phase.

artifacts.summary: 7-phase plan, all phases marked [COMPLETED] with inline deviation annotations
Implementation summary with verification results and full deviation list

decisions_made: extensions.json target: preset-scoped project-root dotfiles via config.lua root_state_file field; legacy state_file field removed entirely (fully unreferenced after state.lua change)
settings.json/settings.local.json: NOT relocated (Claude Code hardcodes .claude/ path); install-once loader semantics + wipe-time backup/restore wrapper implemented as designed

manager.regenerate resets extension state to empty before reloading, rather than iterating manager.load directly against the surviving state -- manager.load's own 'already loaded' guard would otherwise reject every formerly-active extension; the reset lets manager.load's existing recursive dependency resolution rebuild everything correctly regardless of iteration order

post-hoc gap found and closed: manager.unload was deleting settings.json/settings.local.json before install-once could ever apply on the next load, defeating install-once for the manager.reload (unload-then-load) cycle; fixed by excluding those two files from removal via a newly-exported loader_mod.INSTALL_ONCE_ROOT_FILES

restore wired into manager.regenerate, not the picker's 'Load Core' path (sync.load_all_globally does not touch root_files for .claude at all -- settings are loader-owned, not sync-owned, for that base_dir), per the plan's own documented fallback

new config.settings_backup_dir field (preset-scoped, mirroring root_state_file) added for the settings backup staging directory naming, not explicitly named in the original plan text but consistent with its collision-avoidance rationale

logs/ relocated to project-root .agent-logs/ (single shared name, not preset-scoped, per the plan's own wording) across 5 source scripts plus all deployed copies, incidentally converging .opencode/extensions/core/hooks/*.sh (which had pre-existing drift hardcoding .claude/logs) with the deployed .opencode/hooks/*.sh copies

context/index.json's per-entry JSON key ordering is a genuine, pre-existing non-determinism (Lua pairs() iteration order feeding vim.json.encode), confirmed via two independent fresh loads with no wipe involved at all -- out of scope for this task, verified structurally (entry-path set) instead of by byte hash in Phase 7
